findings.description: The authoritative branch is now selected only by `.loa.config.yaml implement_gate.mode: authoritative`, but once selected it still trusts `tool_input.active_skill`, which the header comment itself says is model-authored. Two weaknesses stack: (a) `.loa.config.yaml` lives at the project root, outside the System Zone hook that fences `.claude/`, so the same model the gate is meant to fence can flip the mode with one Write and then self-assert `active_skill: implement` on the next App-Zone write; (b) IG-11 pins the opt-in as undocumented in docs/ and the example config, so an operator who finds it in the hook source gets no warning that it downgrades the fence to self-attestation. The default (heuristic) is strictly safer than the pre-diff auto-detection, so this is not a regression, but the opt-in is a footgun with no harness-side evidence requirement.
findings.failure_mode: An operator (or the model editing the project config) enables authoritative mode; App-Zone writes outside /implement are allowed whenever the tool call JSON carries `active_skill: implement|bug`, silently bypassing the fail-ask fence.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the authoritative branch until a harness-set skill field exists (the evidence recorder can stay), or gate it on both the config key AND a harness-written `platform-features.json` `harness_signal`/`active_skill_available: true` written by detect-platform-features.sh (not by this hook), and document the key with its trust implications in `.loa.config.yaml.example` (dropping the IG-11 'undocumented' assertion).

findings.description: `rule_key` returns 1 for any rule that is not `Bash(...)`. In the allow/deny loaders that is guarded with `|| continue`, but in the requirements loop it is called bare: `rule_key "$perm"`. The script runs under `set -euo pipefail`, so a single non-Bash entry in `all_required` (e.g. a future `Read(...)`/`WebFetch(...)` requirement) aborts the whole checker with no report, no WARN, and a non-zero exit that the preflight will read as 'permissions missing' or as a crash. The old `base_pattern_of` never failed, so this is a new abort path. Latent today if every requirement is `Bash(...)`; also note that for an exact-key requirement `base` becomes `*=foo` (never matches), which is harmless but confirms the function was only designed for wildcard Bash requirements.
findings.failure_mode: Adding a non-Bash rule to the required list makes check-permissions.sh exit silently under errexit on every preflight instead of reporting it as missing.
findings.suggested_fix: `rule_key "$perm" || { missing_permissions+=("$perm"); continue; }` (or `warn` and continue), and compute `base` only when `key` starts with `*`.

findings.cross_file_justification: The recorder now writes `.run/platform-features.json`, a file previously owned by detect-platform-features.sh and consumed by its 1-hour cache check (reviewer concern 2); the writer is in the diff, the readers are in truncated files.
findings.description: When `.run/` exists but `platform-features.json` does not (fresh checkout, or after `.run` cleanup), the recorder creates the file with only `{active_skill_available, active_skill_seen_at, active_skill_source}`. If detect-platform-features.sh treats any sub-1-hour file as a fresh cache and returns early, downstream readers see a file with no `schema_version`, `detected_at`, or `harness_signal` for up to an hour, and `jq -r '.harness_signal // ...'` style consumers get their fallback instead of a real detection. The mktemp+mv write itself is atomic and `${_ig_base:-{\}}` correctly expands to `{}` (bash treats `\}` inside `${...}` as an escaped brace), so there is no quoting or partial-write bug; the concern is purely the schema-less file poisoning the cache. The recorder is also unconditional on file_path (runs for every Write/Edit), which is fine for cost but widens the window.
findings.failure_mode: loa-status / detect-platform-features report 'unknown'/default platform features for an hour after the gate recorder creates the file first, and the recorder's own `active_skill_available: false` may be read as an authoritative detection result.
findings.suggested_fix: Only merge into an existing object (skip when `_ig_base` is empty), or have detect-platform-features.sh treat a file missing `schema_version`/`detected_at` as a cache miss regardless of mtime.

findings.cross_file_justification: The retarget to the `cheap` alias lands on `anthropic:claude-sonnet-5`, whose catalog entry in this diff's `.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml` carries `params.thinking_adaptive: true` and `temperature_supported: false`.
findings.description: The extractor keeps its historical call shape (`30` s, `500` output tokens) but now targets Sonnet 5 with adaptive thinking emitted by the Anthropic adapter. Thinking tokens count against `max_tokens`; a 500-token budget on an adaptive-thinking model can be consumed entirely by the thinking block, returning empty or truncated text where the previous target (gpt-4o-mini, no thinking) returned a complete JSON object. The 30 s bound was sized for a small non-reasoning model as well. The `cheap` alias is also what flatline-scorer uses with `temperature: 0.2`, which the adapter must now drop (temperature_supported false) — same behaviour as Sonnet 4.6, so no regression there.
findings.failure_mode: Transformation-extraction calls return `stop_reason: max_tokens` with no/partial text, the JSON parse fails, and the extractor exits 4 on every learning extraction instead of occasionally.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise the output budget for this call (≥ 4096 is the historical Anthropic floor) or pass `--effort low`/disable thinking for this hop; keep 500 only if the adapter is confirmed to exclude thinking tokens from the cap.

findings.cross_file_justification: The escalated full-file view of `.claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py` asserts a different calibration state for this catalog entry than the diff writes.
findings.description: The diff writes `claude-opus-5-5` as `source: conservative_default`, `calibrated_at: null`, ceiling 180000, and its own hunk of the test file asserts exactly that. The supplied full-file (head) version of the same test module, however, asserts `claude-opus-5-5` IS calibrated (`calibrated_at` truthy, `effective_input_ceiling != 180000`, `basis == "calibrated"`), that it is a foreign-transport calibration with `method: probed_headless` and `measured_input_tokens`, and imports `is_foreign_transport_calibration` (cycle-127). Those tests fail against this diff's catalog. Either the diff is stale relative to the repository head or the escalated file is from a later cycle; the review harness cannot tell which. No `transport`/`method`/`measured_input_tokens`/`reprobe_trigger` keys appear in the v3 schema's `ceilingCalibration` $def in this diff either.
findings.failure_mode: If the head test module is the one that ships, `pytest .claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py` fails on `test_lookup_returns_the_concrete_bound_through_the_gate_path` and `test_a_foreign_transport_calibration_carries_its_provenance` with this catalog entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Rebase the catalog hunk and the test hunk onto the same revision; if cycle-127's probe write is intended, the 5-5 entry needs `calibrated_at`, `transport`, `method: probed_headless`, `measured_input_tokens`, `reprobe_trigger`, and matching `probed_ceiling == effective_input_ceiling`, plus schema additions for those keys.
